analysis.description: This paper introduces a new dynamic programming algorithm called FLOPART, designed for peak detection in sequential data analysis. It addresses limitations of existing algorithms by considering both train and test sets with zero train label errors, while maintaining accuracy. The empirical analysis shows FLOPART is more accurate compared to existing algorithms like GFPOP, LOPART, and BINSEG, offering similar time complexity but with improved accuracy in train and test label errors.

type.justification: The paper provides an empirical analysis showing the accuracy and runtime of the proposed algorithm, FLOPART, compared to existing algorithms like GFPOP and LOPART.
type.quote: We provide an empirical analysis that shows FLOPART has a similar time complexity while being more accurate than the existing algorithms in terms of train and test label errors.

name.quote: Changepoint detection models have become a prominent solution for fields... Newer pruning methods have allowed the algorithm to decrease the number of changepoints assessed, which lowers the time complexity to O(n log n).

name.justification: The paper addresses the problem of changepoint detection by introducing an improved algorithm, FLOPART, which is based on dynamic programming.
name.quote: We propose to resolve these issues by creating a new dynamic programming algorithm, FLOPART, that has zero train label errors, and is able to provide highly accurate predictions on the test set.

name.justification: The primary application of the proposed algorithm is peak detection in sequential data.
name.quote: Peak detection is the problem of differentiating regions with higher counts (peaks) from areas with lower counts (background noise).
